points.text: Teacher models improve quickly; observations may not hold in future
Teacher diversity limited; no analysis by architectural differences
Notation M in Section 3.1 unclear (framework or network)
Figures 1-4 not referenced in main text
Typo at lines 112-113: should be D^target
Boundary between data-centric CoT distillation and general data synthesis unclear
Closed-source teacher traces with limited transparency on prompts and settings; reproducibility
LLM-as-a-Judge filtering not validated against human judgments
Visual and agentic tasks underrepresented (one benchmark each)
OOD transfer pairs not systematically justified
Conclusions tied to specific teacher-student pairs; generalization to new architectures unclear
No comparison with non-data-centric distillation such as logit distillation
Only basic augmentation/selection/mixing methods; no SOTA techniques
No rigorous discussion of when strategies generalize versus task-specific
No quantitative inference efficiency metrics (throughput, latency, memory)
Augmentation vs selection vs mixing confounded by training-set size; no size-matched control
LLM-as-a-Judge effectiveness claims contradicted by own tables
Teacher-correctness filtering consistent-improvement claim contradicted
Recommended augment-filter-mix pipelines never evaluated
No Selection/No Mixing baseline rows inconsistent with Vanilla CoT
Vanilla CoT below No CoT and zero-shot; weak fine-tuning recipe
Table 4 swings suggest training instability, not data volume
Table 4 Vanilla CoT numbers inconsistent with Table 1
No variance, CIs or significance tests; single runs for visual/agentic
Teacher models inconsistently specified across abstract, text and tables
Different teachers and judges per task; cross-task comparison uncontrolled
Textual judge Llama-2-70B weak and outdated
Missing details: judge prompt, thresholds, hyperparameters, dataset sizes, training target
Visual+Agentic average defined only for some rows
Learnability-gap claim over-claimed from single small experiment
Architectural alignment explanation for teacher differences speculative
Prior distillation history claim rests on small uncontrolled differences
Table 3 Llama results only on WebArena
OOD 'consistently improves' claim contradicted by flat/negative rows
OOD gains likely format adaptation; controls missing
GSM8K 80.74 after MATH training irreconcilable with low MATH accuracy
Some OOD pairs are near-distribution
OOD analysis cites Table 4 instead of Table 5
No new method; only existing techniques evaluated
'First benchmark' claim strong; no new eval set or protocol
Benchmarks small and old; teachers dated
Modern long-CoT R1-style distillation not studied
Many typos and errors, including Dsource for Dtarget
Analysis uses hedged, untested mechanistic explanations
